title: IDF Strikes Armed Cells Near Yellow Line; 1 Killed, 19 Ceasefire Violations Documented April 21–May 5
detail: Israeli forces conducted targeted drone strikes on armed Palestinian militant cells approaching the Yellow Line ceasefire boundary in northern Gaza on May 5, 2026, killing at least 1 person and wounding several others according to the Palestinian news agency WAFA. The Foundation for Defense of Democracies and its Long War Journal reported that the IDF had documented 19 ceasefire violations between April 21 and May 5, 2026 — primarily incidents of armed groups approaching Israeli positions along the Yellow Line. The IDF stated the strikes were defensive responses to armed cells advancing on forward positions. Palestinian sources disputed the characterization, saying those killed were civilians. The incidents occurred against a backdrop of stalled disarmament negotiations: Hamas formally rejected the Board of Peace disarmament roadmap in Cairo on May 2, and Israel's security cabinet held closed consultations on war resumption on May 4. UN ASG Khiari had warned that the ceasefire was 'increasingly fragile' with 824+ Palestinians killed since October 2025.

media.caption: IDF documents 19 ceasefire violations April 21–May 5 and strikes armed cells near Yellow Line in northern Gaza

title: Board of Peace Envoy Mladenov Visits Netanyahu; Reports 'Positive' Talks on Trump 20-Point Plan Despite Cairo Impasse
detail: Board of Peace High Representative Nikolay Mladenov traveled to Israel on May 5, 2026, meeting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss implementing the Trump administration's 20-Point Comprehensive Plan for Gaza. Mladenov characterized the discussion as 'positive and substantive,' with both sides reaffirming commitment to the plan. The visit followed the Board of Peace's stalled Cairo talks — Hamas formally rejected the UN-backed disarmament roadmap on May 2 — and reports that the Board had received less than $1 billion of its pledged $17 billion reconstruction fund. Foreign Policy reported the same day that Trump's Gaza plan was stalling, with the US Civil-Military Coordination Center near Gaza slated for possible closure. The fundamental gap remained: Hamas refuses disarmament without a binding Israeli withdrawal and Palestinian statehood guarantee, while Israel refuses those conditions in advance of disarmament. The Mladenov visit was viewed by analysts as an attempt to signal diplomatic momentum but yielded no breakthrough on the core impasse.

media.caption: Trump's Gaza peace plan stalls as Mladenov visits Netanyahu following Hamas rejection of the Board of Peace disarmament roadmap
